html:
The Vishnukundinas were a dynasty of the eastern Deccan, in today's Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, in the 5th and 6th centuries. Much about them is known only from copper plate grants.

They rose as the Vakatakas faded, and their strongest king, Madhava Varma II, ruled the lands between the Godavari and Krishna rivers and fought the Pallavas. Their name may come from Vinukonda, a hill fort in Andhra. Around 624 the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II took their coast, and his brother founded the Eastern Chalukyas at Vengi. The map places their shape further south than their home region.
